newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close up on renewed strong bidding.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close up on renewed strong bidding.

text.p: Caracas stocks finally shook off last week's Brazil-inspired weakness, and roared ahead in strong trade on renewed strong bidding by both foreign and local investors, traders said.
"It looks as though the bolsa is going to keep on rising," Interacciones broker Freddy Zambrano said.
The market's 19-share index ended up 2.52 percent at 9,493.30 points as issues 30 rose, 14 fell and five closed flat.

Trade was boosted to a higher than average 112 million shares, worth 42 billion bolivars ($85 million) by large cross-trades in telephone company CANTV, and strong interest in paints and packaging company Corimon.

CANTV completed the first organized sale of its workers' C shares Wednesday with a cross-trade on the Caracas bolsa of over nine million shares at 2,870 bolivars per share. The stock closed up 95.00 bolivars at 3,115.00.
Traders said interest in Corimon was meanwhile prompted by Monday's decision to convert existing B shares into A shares at the rate of 10:13.5.
Over 20 million Corimon A shares traded, with the stock closing up 2.30 bolivars at 19.80.

"That's very substantial turnover, given that the stock has not yet resumed trade on the New York Stock Exchange, although the company's says it will do so Monday," Primera trader Antonio Neri said. Corimon's American Depositary Receipts were suspended on the NYSE in February last year.
Traders said they expected Corimon to be one of the exchange's most liquid and actively-traded stocks once the B to A conversion is completed.
Merinvest's composite index, which includes CANTV, meanwhile ended up 2.82 percent at 148.17 points.
